details:
Forgotten Space Mission – Every Mission Leaves a Legacy

Team: Shadow Fighters

Forgotten Space Mission is an interactive educational project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It focuses on the stories of abandoned and retired space equipment on the Moon and Mars, reminding us that even when a space mission ends, its contribution to exploration is never forgotten.

What does it do and how does it work?

Our project provides a space-themed interactive experience where users explore the importance of space missions and the equipment left behind. Through interactive mission challenges, users learn about communication systems, solar energy, and planetary protection. The experience encourages users to think about the challenges astronauts and robotic missions face while exploring other worlds.

What are its benefits?

The project makes space science more interesting and accessible, especially for students and young learners. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, problem-solving, and awareness of the technology used in space exploration. It also highlights the importance of understanding and responsibly managing human-made objects left on other planetary bodies.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to inspire people to learn more about the history and future of space exploration. We want users to recognize that retired equipment is not simply forgotten waste; it represents scientific achievements, discoveries, and valuable lessons for future missions. The project promotes awareness of planetary protection and responsible space exploration.

What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed the project as a web-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used a web browser to test the application and Netlify to host and publish it online. The project is designed to be accessible through a web link.

How is the project creative?

The project combines storytelling, space exploration, and interactive learning. Instead of presenting only facts about retired space equipment, it invites users to explore mission-related challenges through an engaging space-themed experience. It connects real space exploration history with educational activities.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered educational value, ease of use, accessibility, creativity, and scientific relevance. We aimed to make the experience understandable for different age groups while keeping the concept connected to real challenges in lunar and Martian exploration. We also considered the importance of planetary protection and the long-term legacy of space missions.

Our message: Every mission leaves a legacy. Even when a mission ends, its contribution to space exploration lives on.
